bull.b: The large, fully recruited NATiV3 trial has reached the final-patient milestone and remains scheduled for a late-2026 readout. This gives Inventiva a defined catalyst for resolving clinical uncertainty and supports potential regulatory preparation if efficacy is confirmed.

Positive Phase II-B histological results provide clinical support for lanifibranor across important MASH endpoints, including fibrosis and disease resolution. These findings strengthen the rationale for the pivotal program and could support differentiation if replicated in Phase III.

The enlarged cash position and completed capital-structure actions provide funding visibility through the expected Phase III readout and potential NDA filing. That runway reduces near-term financing pressure and allows management to focus resources on clinical and regulatory execution.

bear.b: Inventiva remains dependent on external financing because operations generate substantial cash burn and revenue has deteriorated sharply. Continued losses constrain internal investment capacity, increase reliance on capital markets, and make financial execution important alongside clinical progress.

Negative equity combined with materially higher debt weakens financial flexibility and increases the burden on future funding decisions. This capital structure may limit the company’s ability to absorb setbacks or finance development independently if milestones are delayed.

Weight gain, fluid retention, and hemoglobin decline remain meaningful tolerability considerations for lanifibranor. Even if attenuated versus full TZD agonists, these effects could influence prescribing, treatment persistence, and the commercial profile if they are confirmed in Phase III.
